candidates.video_title: Butterflies Taste Food With Their FEET 🦋
candidates.video_description: Butterflies don't use their mouths to taste — they use sensors on their feet to detect sweetness the moment they land. Nature is full of surprises like this. Drop a 🦋 if this blew your mind! #butterfly #nature #animalfacts #didyouknow #interestingfacts #science #shorts
candidates.script: Butterflies taste their food before they even take a single bite — and they do it with their feet. The moment a butterfly lands on a flower or a piece of fruit, tiny chemical sensors on its legs instantly detect whether the surface is sweet or safe to eat. They don't need to touch it with their mouth at all. In fact, a butterfly's sense of taste is nearly 200 times stronger than a human's. So next time you see one casually standing on a flower — it's actually having a full meal. Makes you wonder what your feet would say if they could taste the floor you're walking on right now.

candidates.video_title: The Eiffel Tower Gets TALLER Every Summer 🗼
candidates.video_description: The Eiffel Tower actually grows up to 15 centimeters taller during hot summer months due to thermal expansion of its iron structure. This is a real, measurable phenomenon that engineers account for. Could your favorite landmark be hiding secrets too? #eiffeltower #paris #science #funfacts #didyouknow #thermalexpansion #shorts
candidates.script: The Eiffel Tower is not the same height today as it was yesterday. Every single summer, the iron structure heats up under the sun and expands — growing up to 15 centimeters taller. This isn't a theory, it's a measurable, documented fact caused by thermal expansion. Metal expands when it gets hot, and the Eiffel Tower has over 7,000 tons of iron that all stretch slightly under the summer heat. Then in winter, it shrinks back down. Engineers actually planned for this movement when they built it in 1889. So the next time someone says the Eiffel Tower is 330 meters tall — which summer are they talking about?

candidates.topic: Hot water freezes faster than cold water
candidates.teaser: Soğuk su mu daha hızlı donar, sıcak su mu? Cevap sizi şaşırtacak.
candidates.video_title: Hot Water Freezes FASTER Than Cold Water❄️
candidates.video_description: The Mpemba Effect is a real scientific phenomenon where hot water can freeze faster than cold water under certain conditions — and scientists still debate exactly why. This counterintuitive fact has puzzled researchers for decades. What other everyday 'facts' might actually be wrong? #mpembaeffect #science #physics #didyouknow #funfacts #icescience #shorts
candidates.script: If you put hot water and cold water in the freezer at the same time, which one freezes first? Logic says cold water wins easily. But in reality, hot water can actually freeze faster — and this is called the Mpemba Effect. It was officially named after a Tanzanian student in 1963 who noticed his hot ice cream mix froze before the cold one. Scientists still debate the exact reason — some say evaporation reduces the water mass, others point to dissolved gases escaping. But the effect has been observed and confirmed countless times. So the real question is — how many other things we accept as obvious are quietly wrong?

candidates.topic: The Great Wall of China is not visible from space
candidates.teaser: Uzaydan gözle görülebileceği söylenen o yapı hakkında size yıllarca yalan söylendi.
candidates.video_title: You Were LIED to About the Great Wall of China🚀
candidates.video_description: The claim that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye is one of the most widespread myths in history — even Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei confirmed he couldn't see it. The truth might change how you think about 'common knowledge.' #greatwall #china #space #myths #didyouknow #funfacts #shorts
candidates.script: You've probably heard it a hundred times — the Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space. It's in textbooks, documentaries, even school lessons. There's one problem: it's completely false. The wall is long, sure — over 21,000 kilometers. But it's only about 5 to 8 meters wide. From space, that's like trying to spot a single human hair from two kilometers away. In 2003, Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei specifically looked for it during his mission — and couldn't see it. NASA confirmed the same. So who started this myth — and what other 'facts' did we all memorize that were never actually true?

candidates.topic: Your brain is more active while sleeping
candidates.teaser: Uyurken beyniniz kapanmıyor — aslında o an en yoğun çalışma moduna giriyor.
candidates.video_title: Your Brain Works HARDER While You Sleep 🧠
candidates.video_description: During deep sleep and REM cycles, your brain is actually more electrically active than when you're sitting awake and doing nothing. Sleep isn't rest for the brain — it's prime working hours. This changes everything about how we think about sleep. #brain #sleep #neuroscience #didyouknow #humanbody #funfacts #shorts
candidates.script: When you fall asleep tonight, your brain doesn't switch off — it actually shifts into overdrive. During REM sleep, your brain's electrical activity is nearly identical to when you're fully awake and focused. It's using that time to sort memories, flush out toxic waste proteins, repair neural connections and process emotions from the day. In fact, the brain can only clean itself of certain harmful proteins during sleep — proteins linked to Alzheimer's disease. Missing just one night disrupts this entire system. So sleep isn't laziness — it might be the single most productive thing your brain ever does. Are you really getting enough of it?
